2610.03693.title: Transcriptome-informed multi-modal AI for predicting neoadjuvant therapy response from breast cancer biopsies
2610.03693.paper_summary: Scarcity of labeled data limits development of deep learning biomarkers in oncology. We develop a two-stage AI model predicting pathological complete response (pCR) to neoadjuvant therapy in breast cancer. The first stage learns the transcriptome from histopathology using 8,742 patients across 32 cancer types, corroborated by pathologist review and spatial agreement with measured expression. This simplifies the second stage to predicting pCR from inferred expression and clinical variables. Developed using 1,080 patients (five cohorts) and evaluated in 1,412 patients (nine cohorts), the model achieves a pooled AUROC of 0.79 (95% CI, 0.73-0.85), discriminating responders within molecular subtypes. It outperforms histopathological biomarkers, remaining stable across intratumoral sampling and with minimal biopsy tissue. Ablations show transcriptome-wide inference improves discrimination over clinical variables alone or one-stage pathology models, and robustness by avoiding genomic assays' gene selection constraints. These results indicate that biologically informed compression may generalize to data-sparse applications in precision oncology.
2610.03693.paper_summary_zh: 標記數據的稀缺限制了深度學習生物標記在腫瘤學中的發展。我們開發了一個兩階段的人工智慧模型，預測乳腺癌對新輔助療法的病理完全反應（pCR）。第一階段從32種癌症類型的8,742名患者的組織病理學中學習轉錄組，並經病理學家審查及與測量表達的空間一致性進行驗證。這簡化了第二階段，從推斷的表達和臨床變數中預測pCR。該模型使用1,080名患者（五個隊列）開發，並在1,412名患者（九個隊列）中進行評估，達到0.79的合併AUROC（95% CI, 0.73-0.85），能夠在分子亞型中區分反應者。它的表現優於組織病理學生物標記，並在腫瘤內取樣和最小活檢組織中保持穩定。消融結果顯示，轉錄組範圍的推斷在區分方面優於僅依賴臨床變數或單階段病理模型，並通過避免基因組檢測的基因選擇限制來提高穩健性。這些結果表明，生物學知識驅動的壓縮可能對精準腫瘤學中的數據稀缺應用具有普遍性。
